discrepancies.oldBehaviour: `verify.py list` -> exit 2, `unknown subcommand 'list'`; a bare `verify.py` -> exit 2 with the same message; source carried `args.command or "list"`.
discrepancies.repair: `list` is a real subcommand routed through `emit_listing` and exits 0; the `args.command or "list"` default is replaced by an explicit `None` refusal whose message names the accepted forms. Repaired in the D1-D5 batch at f2ec25379 (evidence/defects/d1-d5/RECEIPT.md).
discrepancies.statement: At a9bcb5480 `--help` called the positional value 'a subcommand name, `all`, or `list`', the unknown-subcommand message listed `list` among the known names, and `main` wrote `name = args.command or "list"`; but no dispatch branch accepted `list`, so `verify.py list` and a bare `verify.py` both printed "unknown subcommand 'list'" and exited 2. The only accepted form was the `--list` flag.
discrepancies.surfaceEffect: command `list` declares `invocation: ["--list"]` and the `list` subcommand probe; the bare word is refused
discrepancies.title: `list` was advertised as a subcommand and refused as one

discrepancies.oldBehaviour: `--list --json` -> exit 0 with TSV, not a JSON object; `verify.py` contained no `LISTING_SCHEMA`.
discrepancies.repair: `listing_rows`, `listing_document`, `render_listing` and `emit_listing` emit the listing document when `--json` is set, in both the `list` and `--list` forms. Repaired in the D1-D5 batch at f2ec25379.
discrepancies.statement: At a9bcb5480 `verify.py --list --json` printed the tab-separated listing and exited 0; no JSON document was emitted, because the listing branch returned before serialisation. The help text described `--json` as 'emit one machine-readable document' with no exception.
discrepancies.surfaceEffect: `list` declares `jsonForm: document` with the listing document's three fields; the discovery block records `emitsJson: true` and the schema
discrepancies.title: `--json` was accepted by the discovery listing and ignored

discrepancies.documentEffect: docs/PUBLIC-VERIFIER.md §2.1 states the precedence rule; §9 records it as documented
discrepancies.oldBehaviour: the precedence existed but no document stated it.
discrepancies.repair: documented as part of the contract (docs/PUBLIC-VERIFIER.md §2.1); no executable change was needed or made.
discrepancies.statement: `--list` takes precedence over `--explain`, which takes precedence over running the named command; `--json`, `--network` and `--tmp` have no effect on `--list` or `--explain`. The behaviour is stable and defensible, but it was in no document, so a caller could not tell which output to expect from `--list --explain`.
discrepancies.surfaceEffect: the precedence is part of the documented contract
discrepancies.title: the argument precedence among the discovery commands was undocumented

witness.observation: `--list --explain` prints the listing, not the explanation blocks

discrepancies.documentEffect: docs/PUBLIC-VERIFIER.md §6 states the derived audited set; §9 records the repair
discrepancies.oldBehaviour: `--explain consumer-curl` printed `private: court, artifacts/phase2/install`; the audited set omitted `install`.
discrepancies.repair: the declaration is removed, because all 155 files under `artifacts/phase2/install` are Git-tracked checkout content with no untracked or ignored entry; and `audited_private_roots()` now derives the audited set from the known roots plus every declared read. Repaired in the D1-D5 batch at f2ec25379.
discrepancies.statement: At a9bcb5480 the three consumer commands declared `artifacts/phase2/install` as a private path, but the interface's audited root set named `artifacts/phase2/shell` instead. The declared path was therefore never counted, so presence-reporting could never report it. A declared private read that presence reporting cannot see is an under-report, not a declaration.
discrepancies.surfaceEffect: the consumer commands declare `court` only; the private-state rule names the derived audited set and no known gap
discrepancies.title: a declared private root was outside the audited root set

discrepancies.documentEffect: docs/PUBLIC-VERIFIER.md §7 states both inputs; §9 records the repair
discrepancies.oldBehaviour: `private_state` carried no `declared` marker; `verify.py` had no `INPUT_KEYS`; the block was compared between runs.
discrepancies.repair: `private_state` is declared as `private-state-input`, required to be present and populated, and excluded from the compared projection alongside `environment`; the detector refuses a document that does not declare it. Repaired in the D1-D5 batch at f2ec25379.
discrepancies.statement: At a9bcb5480 the `environment` block was declared as an input and excluded from the two-run comparison, but `private_state` was a separate top-level block computed from `git status` and was inside the compared record. Two runs over the same checkout therefore differed if an untracked or ignored entry appeared between them, and the published sentence excluded only `environment`.
discrepancies.surfaceEffect: the determinism rule names both inputs and clears `knownGap`
discrepancies.title: live private-state readings sat inside the deterministic record

discrepancies.statement: Found while re-deriving this record. D2 repaired the listing, but `verify.py --explain --json` and `verify.py --help --json` still accept `--json` and print text, emitting no document. The contract states that exception (PUBLIC-VERIFIER.md §2.1, §2.2 and §4) and the surface declares `explain` as `jsonForm: none`, so the declaration and the executable agree; the executable's own `--help` sentence does not name the exception, and an outside caller reading only `--help` would expect a document.
discrepancies.surfaceEffect: `explain` keeps `jsonForm: none`; the declaration is accurate about the executable

contract.0: every selected required step is PASS; a single requested step gates on itself and must be PASS
contract.1: at least one selected step is not PASS: FAIL, BLOCKED or NOT_RUN. NOT_RUN is never a pass
contract.2: the invocation was refused before any step ran: an unknown subcommand, a malformed argument list, or a surface that cannot be read

unknown-command.stderr_head: verify: unknown subcommand 'nosuch-command'; known: manifest, rebuild, proofs, differential, instruments, controls, rece

notes: The listing, the help text and the explain blocks are the executable's own words; nothing here is copied from the declaration.
The JSON field set is read from one probe run; value-level determinism is the separate two-run comparison in the verdict.
A discrepancy is a finding from reading the source, not a shape comparison: the detector cannot see behaviour that leaves the listed surface unchanged.
